data.cultural_impact: The name "Jayyid" signifies having a high moral character and being an exemplary role model for others in the Islamic community. It is a noble name that carries the Middle Eastern cultural heritage of emphasizing excellence, purity, and nobility in individual conduct. This ideal is essential for maintaining harmony within families and fostering a strong sense of community in Islamic societies.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jayyid holds immense spiritual significance in Islam, as it refers to possessing God-consciousness and living up to the standards set by Allah in the Quran.By embracing the qualities of Jayyid, an individual is reflecting the divine attributes of perfection and mercy, and striving for self-improvement and spiritual growth. It is a reminder to constantly cultivate good morals, kind actions, and a humble spirit in one's pursuit of a closer relationship with Allah.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah. Vol. 12, p. 187. The name Jayyid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: During the rule of the Abbasid Caliph Harun Al-Rashid (786-809 AD)
historical_references.context: Jayyid ibn Abd Allah Al-Makki was a famous Qari (Reciter of the Quran) and poet during Harun Al-Rashid's era. He was renowned for his beautiful voice and excellent pronunciation. Once, when the caliph visited Makkah, Jayyid was chosen to lead the Taraweeh prayers in the Grand Mosque.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abdul Hadi, Sharh Nahj Al-Balaghah. Vol. 1, p. 420. The name Jayyid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: During the period of the Rightly Guided Caliphs (632-661 AD)
historical_references.context: Jayyid ibn Sa'd Al-Ansari was a companion of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and a prominent Sahabi (Companion). He was renowned for his excellent character and piety. Once, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) praised him in front of the whole community for his noble qualities.
